title: Demonstrating the Uses of the Novel Gravitational Force Spectrometer to Stretch and Measure Fibrous Proteins
protocol: Submerge about 10 mg of glass or silica beads in 0.04% 3-Aminopropyltriethoxysilane for two minutes.
Rinse with two changes of double distilled water and centrifuge at 2000 X G for 5 minutes.
Discard supernatant.
Add 5 mL of coupling buffer (0.01 M pyridine, pH adjusted to 6.0) and shake vigorously.
Centrifuge as described above.
Repeat the previous two steps three times.
To wet cake of beads, add 2 mL of 5% gluteraldehyde solution and shake vigorously.
Rotate bead/gluteraldehyde mixture for 3 hours at room temperature under a hood.
Centrifuge and aspirate the supernatant.
Wash the beads in 5 mL of coupling buffer by shaking them vigorously and centrifuging, then aspirating the supernatant.
Repeat the previous step three more times.
Add about 15 μL of the desired antibody to beads and shake vigorously.
Rotate the mixture for 16-24 hours under a hood.
Under the hood, add 5 mL of 1 M glycine quenching solution (pH adjusted to 7.0) and shake vigorously.
Rotate this mixture for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge and aspirate the supernatant.
Add 5 mL of wash buffer (0.01 M Tris, pH 7.0; 0.1% sodium azide; 0.1% BSA; 0.15 M NaCl; and 0.001 M EDTA) and shake vigorously.
Centrifuge and aspirate the supernatant.
Repeat the previous step three additional times.
Change buffer to low-salt buffer (0.1 M KCl; 0.02 M imidazole; 5 mM MgCl2; adjust to pH 7.0).
Repeat buffer change three times.
Take a small amount of prepared beads and add them to a microcentrifuge tube with assay buffer.
Reduce protein concentration to around 5 μM using the assay buffer.
Prepare at least a total volume of 400 μL including buffer, protein, and beads.
Rotate mixture at approximately 1 RPM for 3 hours.
Coat a thick microscope slide with 0.01% nitrocellulose in amyl acetate.
Let the coated slide dry for about 10 minutes.
Cut cover slides to make four strips of glass using vacuum grease on both sides of the edge.
Press grease-coated strips onto dried nitrocellulose-covered slide to create a box.
Pipette approximately 2 μL of bead/protein mixture into the chamber created by the glass strips.
Add about 20-400 μL of low-salt buffer depending on chamber size.
Press a cover slip on top of the chamber coated with vacuum grease.
Let slide sit on a level place so the beads have ample time to anchor themselves to the nitrocellulose.
Mount slide onto GFS stage.
Monitor what the GFS camera is recording and search for legitimate "bead pairs."
Go through the depth of focus to determine if the "mobile" bead is not resting on the surface of the slide.
Note angle mobile bead is away from dmax (dmax = the maximum distance between the centroids of the coupled microspheres).
Move the scope into position to acquire video.
RECORD as the pair travels from dmin to dmax and back to dmin.
Shoot a movie of the background so it can be subtracted later for analysis.
If performing a GFS drop, move the scope back to dmax.
Record the drop at at least 60 frames per second.
Transform raw video into digitally "thresholded" image.
Run macro in ImageJ to determine the centroid position of each bead in every frame of video.
Dump the X,Y and area data from ImageJ into Excel.
Plot the points.
Determine the radius of each bead precisely in ImageJ.

Input the radius and other relevant data into the nested equation: \(d = [(g \sin \alpha)^2 + (g \cos \alpha + d_{\text{max}} - g)^2]^{\frac{1}{2}}\) where \(g = [d_{\text{min}}^2 + r_b^2 - (r_a + r_b)^2]^{\frac{1}{2}} = r_b \sin \beta\).
Calculate the buoyancy force using the fitted radius of the mobile bead.
Subtract the buoyancy force from the total force to obtain the net force imparted by the mobile bead on the molecule in piconewtons.
Measure the absolute length of the tethered molecule between antibody attachments in nanometers.
Use the formula \(F = V (d-b) a\) where \(F\) is the force, \(V\) is the volume of the bead, \(d\) is the density of the glass microsphere, and \(a\) is the acceleration due to gravity.
Minimize vibrations as much as possible during bead preparation.
Let the sealed flow chamber stand for about five minutes on a level table after construction.
Allow any unattached larger beads to float down through the buffer and rest in the layer of nitrocellulose.
Put the identified bead pair through a preliminary rotation.
Monitor the behavior of the bead pair during rotation.
Ensure the large bead is firmly affixed to the slide.
Exclude the bead pair if the anchored bead rolls or is unstable.
Evaluate acquired data using a plot of bead separation distances versus change in angle relative to gravity.
Identify a good representative result showing little separation on a plateau and increasing separation until reaching dmax before returning to baseline dmin.
Cull improper bead pairs at various stages during processing, shooting, and analyzing.
